description: Packaging and running software with containers and orchestrating it with Kubernetes: how containers isolate processes, building images with Dockerfiles, container networking and storage, the Kubernetes control plane, pods, deployments and services, configuration, secrets and autoscaling, and systematic troubleshooting of broken clusters. Practised hands-on in simulated terminals and a simulated multi-node cluster in the browser, taught to the depth of the Kubernetes administrator and developer certifications.
modelledOn: Burns, Beda, Hightower and Evenson, Kubernetes: Up and Running
CNCF Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) and Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) curricula
Open Container Initiative image and runtime specifications
outcomes: Explain how containers use namespaces, control groups and layered file systems and contrast them with virtual machines.
Write efficient, secure Dockerfiles and multi-container applications and publish images to a registry.
Configure container networking and persistent storage for stateful and stateless workloads.
Describe the Kubernetes architecture and deploy applications with pods, deployments, services and ingress.
Manage configuration, secrets, resource limits and autoscaling and perform rolling updates and rollbacks.
Diagnose and repair failing workloads, nodes and cluster networking using a systematic troubleshooting method.

units.title: Containers and images
topics: Why containers: dependency hell, environment drift, density; containers versus virtual machines
Linux foundations: namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, seccomp, union and overlay file systems
The OCI image format: layers, manifests, digests and tags; registries and pulling by digest
Container runtimes: Docker Engine, containerd, runc and Podman; rootless containers
The container life cycle: run, exec, logs, inspect, stop, remove; restart policies

units.title: Writing Dockerfiles
topics: Dockerfile instructions: FROM, RUN, COPY, ENV, ARG, WORKDIR, USER, EXPOSE, ENTRYPOINT versus CMD
Layer caching and build order; .dockerignore; multi-stage builds for small images
Choosing base images: distroless, Alpine and slim images; image size on slow and metered connections
Image security: running as non-root, pinning versions, scanning for vulnerabilities, signing images
Containerising a Node.js API and a Python service; Docker Compose for multi-container development

units.title: Container networking and storage
topics: Bridge, host and overlay networks; port publishing; DNS-based service discovery between containers
Network namespaces and virtual Ethernet pairs; inspecting traffic between containers
Volumes, bind mounts and tmpfs; data that must survive a container
Running a database in a container: persistence, backups and why it is often a bad idea in production

units.title: Kubernetes architecture
topics: Why orchestration: scheduling, self-healing, scaling, rolling updates; the declarative model and reconciliation loops
Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager, cloud controller manager
Worker nodes: kubelet, kube-proxy, the container runtime interface
Setting up a cluster with kubeadm; managed clusters on EKS, AKS and GKE; lightweight k3s for low-cost hardware
kubectl, kubeconfig, contexts and namespaces; reading and writing YAML manifests

units.title: Pods, deployments and services
topics: Pods: multi-container patterns (sidecar, init containers, ambassador), pod life cycle, probes for liveness, readiness and startup
ReplicaSets and Deployments; rolling updates, rollout history and rollbacks
StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs and CronJobs
Services: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, headless services; endpoints and EndpointSlices
Ingress and the Gateway API; TLS termination; exposing a mobile money payment API through an ingress controller

units.title: Configuration, secrets and scaling
topics: ConfigMaps and Secrets as environment variables and mounted files; encryption of secrets at rest; external secret stores
Resource requests and limits; quality of service classes; LimitRanges and ResourceQuotas
Scheduling: node selectors, affinity and anti-affinity, taints and tolerations, topology spread
Autoscaling: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, Vertical Pod Autoscaler, cluster autoscaler; metrics server
Persistent storage: PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses and dynamic provisioning
Packaging applications with Helm charts and Kustomize overlays

units.title: Cluster security and networking
topics: Authentication and RBAC: service accounts, roles, role bindings, least privilege
Pod Security Standards and admission control; security contexts
The pod network model; CNI plugins such as Calico and Cilium; NetworkPolicies for isolation
Cluster DNS with CoreDNS; service meshes in brief

units.title: Troubleshooting clusters
topics: A troubleshooting method: observe, hypothesise, test, fix, verify; reading events and describe output
Failing workloads: CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, pending pods and unschedulable nodes
Failing networking: services without endpoints, DNS failures, NetworkPolicy mistakes, ingress misrouting
Failing nodes and control plane: NotReady nodes, kubelet logs, certificate expiry, etcd backup and restore
Logging and monitoring a cluster with Prometheus, Grafana and centralised logs
Capstone: deploy, scale, secure and repair a multi-service application on a broken cluster under timed conditions

schedule.title: Why containers and how images work
schedule.exercise: Explain in half a page how a container differs from a virtual machine, and trace what happens in the kernel when a container starts.

tasks.title: Run an Alpine container, list its processes and compare with the host process list to show process isolation
Limit a container to 64 MB of memory and 0.5 CPU, then run a memory stress command and confirm the container is killed at the limit
Inspect an image manifest, list its layers and digests, then pull the same image by digest and by tag and show they match

schedule.title: Container runtimes and lifecycle
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page runbook for starting, inspecting, restarting and removing a service container, including the restart policy you chose and why.

tasks.title: Run, exec into, read logs of, stop and remove an nginx container using the lifecycle commands in order and record each exit status
Configure restart policies on three containers, kill the processes in each and record which ones come back and after how long
Run a container as a rootless user, show its UID mapping on the host and explain which privileged operations fail

schedule.title: Writing efficient and safe Dockerfiles
schedule.exercise: Review a given 1 GB Dockerfile and write a list of changes that would shrink it and make it safer, ordered by impact.

tasks.title: Write a Dockerfile for a small Node.js API using FROM, COPY, ENV, WORKDIR and CMD, build it and curl the running container
Reorder instructions and add a dockerignore file to a Python Dockerfile so that a code change rebuilds only two layers, and show the cache hits
Convert a given Dockerfile to a multi-stage build on a slim base with a non-root user, pinned versions and a scan with no critical findings

schedule.title: Container networking and storage
schedule.exercise: Draw the network and volume layout for a web app with a database, and explain what survives when each container is deleted.

tasks.title: Create a user-defined bridge network, attach two containers and make one reach the other by name while a port is published to the host
Run a database with a named volume, insert 10 rows, delete the container, start a new one on the same volume and verify the rows
Inspect the veth pairs and network namespace of two containers, capture traffic between them and diagnose why a third isolated container cannot connect

schedule.title: Kubernetes architecture
schedule.exercise: Label a diagram of the control plane and a worker node, and narrate what each component does when a user applies a deployment.

tasks.title: Deploy an app with three replicas, delete one pod, and observe the reconciliation loop recreate it, recording the event sequence
Map each step of kubectl apply to the API server, etcd, scheduler and controller manager and verify against the cluster event log
Cordon and drain a worker node, trace what the kubelet does to the pods and show them rescheduled onto other nodes

schedule.title: Clusters and kubectl
schedule.exercise: Compare a kubeadm cluster, a managed cluster and k3s for a small clinic network with limited hardware, and recommend one.

tasks.title: Create two namespaces, switch contexts with kubectl and deploy the same pod into each, listing resources per namespace
Bring up a three-node cluster in the console, join a new worker node and verify all nodes report Ready
Write a manifest for a pod from scratch, apply it, fix three seeded YAML errors in a broken one and describe each failure message

schedule.title: Pods, deployments and jobs
schedule.exercise: Design the Kubernetes objects for a web app, a nightly report job and a database, and justify each object kind.

tasks.title: Add liveness and readiness probes to a pod and show traffic withheld while the readiness probe fails
Perform a rolling update of a deployment from v1 to v2 with maxUnavailable 1, then roll back to v1 using rollout history
Create a CronJob running every minute, a StatefulSet of three replicas and a DaemonSet, and verify pod names and node placement for each

schedule.title: Services and ingress
schedule.exercise: Write the routing table for an ingress exposing a mobile money payment API and a web admin site, with TLS on both.

tasks.title: Expose a deployment through ClusterIP, NodePort and LoadBalancer services and curl each from inside and outside the cluster
Find why a service has zero endpoints because of a label mismatch and fix it so traffic reaches all three pods
Create an ingress with host and path rules routing two services and terminate TLS with a given certificate, then verify with three requests

schedule.title: Configuration, resources and scheduling
schedule.exercise: Plan resource requests and limits for four services on a three-node cluster and explain the QoS class each one receives.

tasks.title: Inject configuration into a pod using a ConfigMap as environment variables and a Secret as a mounted file, and print both from inside the pod
Set requests and limits on three pods, run an overuse test and identify which pod is OOMKilled and which QoS class it has
Spread six replicas across three nodes using anti-affinity and taints and tolerations, so database pods run only on tainted nodes

schedule.title: Autoscaling, storage and packaging
schedule.exercise: Describe how you would package an app for three environments using Kustomize overlays, and what differs between them.

tasks.title: Configure a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler at 50 percent CPU, generate load and record replica counts over time as it scales up and down
Create a PersistentVolumeClaim with a storage class, mount it in a pod, delete the pod and verify the data survives in the replacement
Create Kustomize overlays for dev and prod with different replica counts and image tags and verify the rendered manifests differ as intended

schedule.title: Cluster security and networking
schedule.exercise: Write a least-privilege access policy for a developer, a CI bot and a read-only auditor on one cluster.

tasks.title: Create a service account and a role allowing only get and list on pods, bind it and test that deleting a pod is denied
Write a NetworkPolicy so the database accepts traffic only from the API pods and test allowed and blocked connections
Fix a deployment rejected by Pod Security Standards by adding a security context with non-root user and dropped capabilities, then verify it starts

schedule.title: Troubleshooting workloads and networking
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page troubleshooting checklist from observed symptom to likely cause for five common failure states.

tasks.title: Use describe and events to find why a pod is Pending and fix it by correcting the resource request
Diagnose and fix three broken pods (ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled) and record the evidence that identified each cause
Repair a cluster where DNS fails, a service has no endpoints and a NetworkPolicy blocks traffic, restoring a working request path end to end

schedule.title: Nodes, observability and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write the post-incident report for the capstone repair, including timeline, root causes and prevention steps.

tasks.title: Deploy Prometheus and a dashboard, create an alert on pod restarts above 3 and trigger it by crashing a pod
Recover a cluster with a NotReady node and an expired certificate by reading kubelet logs, renewing the certificate and restoring etcd from a backup
Deploy, scale to five replicas, secure with RBAC and a NetworkPolicy, and repair a three-service app on a broken cluster within a 45-minute limit
